title: Private Upgrades Beta Plan (VPC + On-Prem): Candidate Customers, Prereqs, Comms, Success Metrics, Schedule
content:
Doc purpose
- Coordinate 1–2 beta customers for the first supported end-to-end Redwood Private upgrade + rollback workflow (VPC and on-prem/air-gapped).
- Ensure we have: (a) the right candidates, (b) clear prerequisites, (c) a comms + support plan, and (d) measurable success criteria.

Beta scope (what we are validating)
- Installer-driven upgrade orchestration with prechecks, backups, deterministic upgrade ordering, health gates, and rollback hooks.
- Operator UX: interactive + non-interactive modes, clear remediation hints, JSON output for Support ingestion.
- Observability + diagnostics: correlation id, step timings, bundle collection, and the triage path.

Non-goals for beta
- Forcing “zero downtime” upgrades in every environment. We do require “predictable, bounded maintenance window” + safe sequencing.
- Supporting arbitrary downgrade across forward-only DB schema migrations (must be enforced/guardrailed).

Owners / roles
- Beta pilots lead: Markus Klein (Solutions/PS)
- Release orchestration + cutover: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
- Control plane + upgrade APIs: Ethan Park
- SRE runbook + on-call readiness: Rafael Mendes / Sean Gallagher
- Support enablement + triage workflow: Dev Patel / Owen Phillips
- Security review sign-off for bundles/signing: Marcus Lin / Dr. Aisha Rahman
- PM approvals + customer selection: Vivek Kulkarni

Candidate customers (proposed)
NOTE: Use customer code names in this doc; the CRM links are the source of truth.

Candidate A — “VPC-Alpha” (HubSpot:company_10503)
- Deployment: Private VPC (managed Kubernetes).
- Motivation: scheduled major upgrade already planned; high willingness to do maintenance window + rehearsal.
- Risk level: medium (has historical migration-related failure modes; see SUP-1842).
- What we want to validate here:
  - Snapshot permissions + backup verification on VPC infrastructure.
  - Upgrade sequencing (control plane → gateways → runtime) and readiness gates.
  - Rollback path when a mid-upgrade step fails (simulate failure injection if feasible).

Candidate B — “OnPrem-Airgapped” (HubSpot:company_10441)
- Deployment: on-prem Kubernetes, air-gapped environment.
- Motivation: procurement/security gating is driven by “offline upgrade bundle + signing verification + rollback story.”
- Risk level: high (artifact delivery constraints; more moving pieces outside Redwood control).
- What we want to validate here:
  - Offline bundle import workflow (manifest parsing, signature verification, and failure UX).
  - Upgrade runbook usability without live Redwood connectivity.
  - Diagnostics collection and support escalation when logs must be transferred out-of-band.

Selection criteria (must-have)
- Customer agrees to:
  - A defined maintenance window (≥ 2 hours for first beta; adjust down after rehearsal results).
  - A named operator + backup operator on the call (and ability to run commands / access kubeconfig).
  - Sending a precheck report at least 5 business days before the window.
  - Allowing Redwood to schedule a rollback drill (either real or simulated) once during beta.

Customer prerequisites (checklist)
These are gating: if any fail, we reschedule rather than “try anyway.”

1) Technical prerequisites (both VPC + on-prem)
- Kubernetes:
  - Supported k8s version per installer precheck (customer must meet minimum; no exceptions in beta).
  - Cluster access available during window (kubeconfig/role binding ready).
- Capacity:
  - Nodes have headroom for rolling restarts (documented minimum free CPU/mem).
  - Disk free space meets backup + log bundle requirements (precheck validates; customer must remediate if below threshold).
- Storage:
  - Default storage class is set + supports required volume operations.
  - PV snapshot capability confirmed if enabled (optional for beta unless customer requires PV snapshots).
- Permissions:
  - Service account / IAM permissions for snapshots + reads/writes to backup target.
- Version compatibility:
  - Customer is on a supported “from” version for the chosen “to” version (installer must validate).
- Change control:
  - Customer change ticket/approval process completed before the beta window.

2) Backup prerequisites
- Control plane DB snapshot target configured and reachable.
- Backup verification enabled (we require verify step in beta; no “snapshot only”).
- Retention: minimum 2 verified backups retained until 2 weeks after upgrade.

3) Security prerequisites
- Artifact verification is mandatory:
  - VPC: signed artifacts verified during install/upgrade.
  - On-prem air-gapped: offline bundle signature verification required; customer must provide allowed import path.
- Audit logging:
  - Ensure audit events for upgrade/rollback actions are enabled and retained through beta.

4) Operational prerequisites
- Customer confirms:
  - How they will monitor service health during the window (their APM + Redwood dashboards).
  - Who has authority to approve rollback if issues arise.

Comms plan

1) Internal comms
- Slack channels:
  - #eng-private-deployments for day-to-day
  - #eng-releases for go/no-go and release coordination
  - #eng-sre for monitoring/on-call readiness
  - #support for support enablement + escalation drills
- Internal go/no-go 48 hours prior:
  - Attendees: Markus, Connor, Ethan, Rafael (SRE), Dev Patel (Support), Marcus Lin (Security if on-prem).
  - Output: final runbook link, roles assigned, escalation tree confirmed.

2) Customer comms
- T-10 business days: Beta kickoff call
  - Confirm target versions, environment constraints, maintenance window, stakeholders.
- T-5 business days: Precheck report due
  - Redwood reviews results, returns remediation list within 1 business day.
- T-2 business days: Final readiness + window confirmation
  - Confirm backup target, artifact availability, and rollback decision-maker.
- T+1 business day: Post-upgrade debrief + action items

Call structure for the upgrade window
- One video bridge + one “ops-only” chat (customer operator + Redwood).
- Roles:
  - Command driver (Customer operator)
  - Redwood narrator / runbook driver (Rafael or Markus)
  - Release Eng observer for tool behavior + logging (Connor or Devon)
  - Support observer for diagnostics realism (Dev Patel or Owen)
- Hard stops:
  - If prechecks fail: stop.
  - If backup verify fails: stop.
  - If upgrade health gate fails and remediation does not resolve within 30 minutes: rollback decision point.

Success metrics (beta)
We will track per-customer and overall.

Must-hit (beta exit criteria)
- Precheck:
  - Precheck completes and produces a readable human summary + machine-readable JSON.
  - All failures include remediation hints that a customer operator can act on without Redwood code changes.
- Backup:
  - Control plane DB snapshot + verification completes successfully.
  - Verification output is logged and included in diagnostics bundle.
- Upgrade:
  - Upgrade completes with no data loss and services reach “healthy” state per runbook.
  - End-to-end time within planned maintenance window (initial target: ≤ 120 minutes).
- Rollback:
  - At least one rollback drill (real rollback OR controlled failure injection → rollback) completes and restores to prior known-good state.
  - Rollback safety checks correctly block rollback when forward-only migrations are detected (if applicable); user messaging must be explicit.
- Observability/supportability:
  - Upgrade correlation id appears in control plane logs and installer logs.
  - Diagnostics bundle is generated and contains: precheck report, step timings, relevant k8s events, and recent pod logs.

Nice-to-have
- Reduction of maintenance window estimate to ≤ 90 minutes for VPC customer by the second attempt.
- Minimal manual steps (goal: no more than 3 “operator choices” beyond confirming prompts).

Beta risks + mitigations
- Backup duration exceeds window (especially on large DBs)
  - Mitigation: do a backup timing rehearsal outside the maintenance window; consider incremental snapshot if supported.
- Snapshot permissions/IAM surprises (VPC)
  - Mitigation: require a permissions precheck + explicit “snapshot dry-run” step.
- On-prem artifact delivery issues
  - Mitigation: offline bundle import test at least 1 week prior, with signature verification.
- Downgrade semantics unclear for customers
  - Mitigation: scripted explanation in the kickoff + explicit written “what rollback means / doesn’t mean” section sent ahead.

Proposed schedule (draft)
(Actual dates will be confirmed after precheck pass and customer approvals.)

Customer: VPC-Alpha
- Kickoff call: Week of 2025-02-10
- Precheck run + report due: 2025-02-14
- Readiness review + go/no-go: 2025-02-18
- Upgrade window #1 (primary): 2025-02-20 19:00–21:00 customer local time
- Buffer window (if reschedule): 2025-02-25 19:00–21:00
- Post-upgrade debrief: 2025-02-21

Customer: OnPrem-Airgapped
- Kickoff call: Week of 2025-02-24
- Offline bundle delivery + import test: by 2025-03-03
- Precheck run + report due: 2025-03-05
- Readiness review + go/no-go: 2025-03-07
- Upgrade window #1 (primary): 2025-03-11 09:00–12:00 (longer window reserved)
- Buffer window (if reschedule): 2025-03-18 09:00–12:00
- Post-upgrade debrief: 2025-03-12

Runbook + tooling readiness checklist (internal)
- Runbook is complete and reviewed by SRE + Support (ENG-2323)
- Installer build is signed and verification behavior is tested (artifact signing standard)
- Offline bundle manifest schema locked for beta (no breaking changes mid-beta)
- Upgrade telemetry dashboards available (upgrade step success/failure counts; step duration)
- Incident tagging workflow enabled for upgrade-related events

Open questions (need answers before locking dates)
- For on-prem: what is the customer-approved mechanism to transfer diagnostics bundles to Redwood (SFTP, ticket attachment, secure portal)?
- Do we require PV snapshots for either customer, or is control plane DB + config sufficient for beta?
- What is our exact rollback window policy for beta (e.g., “rollback supported if within X hours and no forward-only migrations applied”)?

Next actions
- Markus: confirm candidate availability and stakeholder list (by 2025-02-10)
- Vivek: approve customer selection + success criteria wording (by 2025-02-10)
- Connor/Devon: confirm installer build + flags for beta, and provide exact command sequence for runbook (by 2025-02-14)
- Rafael/Sean: finalize monitoring checklist + rollback decision points (by 2025-02-14)
- Dev Patel: confirm Support intake flow for JSON precheck + diagnostics bundles (by 2025-02-18)
- Marcus Lin: sign off on offline bundle verification + key custody expectations for on-prem beta (by 2025-03-01)
